target.title: fix(llm): preserve non-array tool result replay text
target.body:
## Summary

Fix a defensive gap in tool-result replay extraction after #97742: provider replay should preserve useful text when a tool-result content value reaches the shared extractor as a plain string, a single structured object, or a text-like object instead of the canonical content-block array.

## Problem

`extractToolResultText()` currently assumes an array-shaped content value. If a plain string reaches the helper, JavaScript iteration walks individual characters, each character is skipped as a primitive block, and replay text becomes empty. That can make a successful tool execution appear as empty output to the next model turn.

## Changes

- Normalize non-array tool-result content before extraction.
- Preserve primitive string/number/boolean/bigint content as replay text.
- Preserve text-like fields (`text`, `output`, `content`) on non-standard object results.
- Keep structured single-object fallback serialization/redaction behavior.
- Add focused regression coverage for plain string, single object, and text-like object content shapes.

## Validation

- Draft PR: GitHub Actions should be treated as the authoritative validation source for this branch.
- Local focused validation was attempted for `src/llm/providers/tool-result-text.test.ts` and `git diff --check`, but the current investigation environment is affected by the tool-result replay issue and did not provide reliable readable command output.

## Risk

Low. The change broadens accepted input shapes at the replay-helper boundary and keeps existing array-shaped, media-only, explicit text, structured fallback, truncation, and redaction behavior intact.

## Related

- Follow-up to #97742.
